messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (n=10). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (n=10). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sided test? Usually t-test for difference of means. We'll compute mean, variance, pooled variance, t-statistic, degrees of freedom (df= n1+n2-2 = 18). Then compute two-tailed p-value. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: we need variance. Compute each deviation squared.

Compute deviations: 12-23.7 = -11.7; square = 136.89
15-23.7 = -8.7; sq = 75.69
18-23.7 = -5.7; sq = 32.49
20-23.7 = -3.7; sq = 13.69
22-23.7 = -1.7; sq = 2.89
25-23.7 = 1.3; sq = 1.69
28-23.7 = 4.3; sq = 18.49
30-23.7 = 6.3; sq = 39.69
32-23.7 = 8.3; sq = 68.89
35-23.7 = 11.3; sq = 127.69

Sum of squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So sum of squared deviations = 518.10. Sample variance s1^2 = 518.10/(n1-1)=518.10/9=57.5667. Standard deviation s1 = sqrt(57.5667)=7.590.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. So mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Compute deviations: 14-24.9 = -10.9; sq = 118.81
17-24.9 = -7.9; sq = 62.41
19-24.9 = -5.9; sq = 34.81
21-24.9 = -3.9; sq = 15.21
23-24.9 = -1.9; sq = 3.61
26-24.9 = 1.1; sq = 1.21
29-24.9 = 4.1; sq = 16.81
31-24.9 = 6.1; sq = 37.21
33-24.9 = 8.1; sq = 65.61
36-24.9 = 11.1; sq = 123.21

Sum of squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. So sum of squared deviations = 478.90. Sample variance s2^2 = 478.90/9 = 53.2111. Standard deviation s2 = sqrt(53.2111)=7.295.

Now compute pooled variance: Sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (518.1003 + 478.8999)/18 = 997.0002/18 = 55.389. Actually 997/18 = 55.3889. So Sp = sqrt(55.389)=7.44.

Standard error of difference: SE = Sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.44 * 0.4472136 = 3.327.

Difference in means: mean_B - mean_A = 24.9 - 23.7 = 1.2. So t = (mean_B - mean_A)/SE = 1.2 / 3.327 = 0.3607.

Degrees of freedom df = 18. Two-tailed p-value: p = 2 * (1 - CDF_t(|t|)). For t=0.3607, df=18. We can approximate using t distribution. For small t, p ~ 0.72? Let's compute more precisely. Use t distribution table: For df=18, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is 2.101. Our t=0.361 < 2.101, so not significant. For alpha=0.01, t critical is 2.878. Not significant. p-value: we can approximate using t distribution. For t=0.36, df=18, p ~ 0.72? Let's approximate using t distribution formula or use approximate normal: For large df, t approximates normal. For t=0.36, normal two-tailed p = 2*(1 - Phi(0.36)) = 2*(1 - 0.6406) = 2*0.3594 = 0.7188. For df=18, p slightly larger maybe 0.72. So p ~ 0.72.

Thus both tests fail to reject null at alpha 0.05 and 0.01.
